neighbours.label: the step where someone builds on existing work and extends it: the connective after 'build on it' / 'borrow from it' introducing the improvement ('build on it, and improve it', 'while adding')
fire: Each student took the previous draft, built on it, and added a new chapter.
Open-source projects let anyone fork the code and extend it with new features.
The chef learned her mother's recipes and then gave each one her own twist.
Later scientists built on Newton's laws while extending them to new problems.
Musicians sample older songs, rework them, and layer new melodies on top.
The second architect kept the original plan but enlarged it with two new wings.
Every version of the game builds on the last one and adds more levels.
We copy what works for our rivals and then try to improve on it.
quiet: Each student read the previous draft carefully and handed it back.
Open-source projects let anyone download the code and run it for free.
The chef cooked her mother's recipes exactly as they were written.
Later scientists studied Newton's laws in school like everyone else.
Musicians listen to older songs on the radio on long drives.
The second architect looked at the original plan and approved it.
Every version of the game costs the same and runs on old computers.
We watch our rivals closely and note what they sell each month.

notes: Top: 'build on it, and improve it', 'fork it, and so on', 'built on her work, while bringing her own aesthetic', 'copy what works, then try to do a little more'. Probe: 0.53 and 0.66, plain list 0.02. Near misses keep the topic but the prior work is only used or copied, not extended. The + pole is 'but' marking same-X-but-different-Y.
